title: Pwyll and the Otherworld
subtitle: Welsh tales make rulership meet enchantment

learningObjectives.text: What does Arawn ask Pwyll to do?
Why does Arawn forbid a second blow?

main.author: various Welsh traditions
main.locator: The First Branch, Arawn asks Pwyll to defeat Hafgan; local text normalized characters 368527-368896
main.excerpt: One year from this night,” he answered, “is the time fixed between him and me that we should meet at the Ford; be thou there in my likeness, and with one stroke that thou givest him, he shall no longer live. And if he ask thee to give him another, give it not, how much soever he may entreat thee, for when I did so, he fought with me next day as well as ever before.”
main.note: Verbatim Guest translation excerpt; whitespace normalized. Lesson interpretation is separate.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Arawn, king of Annwvyn, asks Pwyll to fight Hafgan at the Ford after a year. Pwyll must take Arawn’s shape and give Hafgan only one blow; a second blow would let him recover.

narrativeBlocks.title: Arawn's terms
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Guest translation; whitespace normalized): “One year from this night,” he answered, “is the time fixed between him and me that we should meet at the Ford; be thou there in my likeness, and with one stroke that thou givest him, he shall no longer live. And if he ask thee to give him another, give it not, how much soever he may entreat thee, for when I did so, he fought with me next day as well as ever before.””

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: The test is not just whether Pwyll can win a fight. He must keep the agreement's exact limit, even when his opponent asks for another blow.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the Mabinogion's Welsh tale of Pwyll and Arawn. Keep the otherworld setting and the tale's rule about a single blow attached to this version.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Track the promise through the exchange: what Pwyll owes Arawn, what he is forbidden to do, and how restraint changes the result.

quiz.prompt: What does Arawn ask Pwyll to do?

choices.text: Take Arawn's shape and defeat Hafgan with one blow at the Ford after a year
Defeat Arawn in a contest for Dyved
Marry Hafgan's daughter and surrender Annwvyn

quiz.explanation: Arawn offers friendship if Pwyll takes his form, meets Hafgan at the Ford, and gives only one blow.

suggestedQuestions: What does this one text not establish?

quiz.prompt: Why does Arawn forbid a second blow?

choices.text: A second blow would break Pwyll's disguise
The Ford can be crossed only once
Hafgan would recover and fight again the next day

quiz.explanation: Arawn explains that Hafgan fought as well as before after receiving a second blow.
